rationale: Verified reviewed commit 44e6cf2f with git show --stat and full-patch inspection. The commit is confined to the three disclosed cleanup surfaces: one decision-table label reword in internal/panel/gate.go, the twin ordering-comment rewords in internal/complete/panel_advisory.go, and deletion of the unreferenced residualDirtyPaths helper from internal/complete/complete.go. No live control flow, gate predicate, materialization protocol, or test behavior changes. The disclosed CompleteBead msg branch is genuinely unreachable in production because internal/complete/complete.go is the sole production caller and always passes an empty message; its removal would touch the shared Executor signature/mock and associated tests, so deferring that harmless dead-branch cleanup to a follow-up bead is an acceptable scope disposition. My prior APPROVE verdict therefore stands.

findings.title: Round-5 fix is confined to the disclosed twin-site prose and dead helper
findings.evidence: git show 44e6cf2f --stat reports exactly three files, 14 insertions and 43 deletions. Full-patch inspection shows a one-line gate label reword, four retired-ordering narration corrections in panel_advisory.go, and deletion of the 31-line residualDirtyPaths function. rg finds no remaining residualDirtyPaths reference.

findings.title: The unreachable CompleteBead auto-commit branch does not block this bead
findings.evidence: Production-only search finds CompleteBead declarations in the Executor interface, mock, and MindspecExecutor plus one caller at internal/complete/complete.go:1099; that caller passes msg="". Thus the msg != "" branch is unreachable through the production workflow. It makes no false runtime claim and has no effect on the reviewed protocol, while deleting it cleanly may entail shared seam and test changes beyond this narrow round-4 dispatch.

findings.title: R5 standing approval remains valid
findings.evidence: Commit 44e6cf2f changes no live protocol behavior. The exact-tree race closure, closed stage discriminator, ADR ordering, regression fixtures, and quality evidence underlying R5's round-2 approval remain untouched, as do the prose-only corrections accepted in rounds 3 and 4.
